deepDives.title: Regasco to roll back LPG prices on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026
deepDives.summary: Regasco is set to implement another price rollback for its liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) products this month, following the movement in international contract prices.
reasons: reader relevance 3/3: LPG price rollback from Nov 19 lowers household cooking costs

article.text:
Republic Gas Corporation (REGASCO) is set to implement another price rollback for its liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) products this month, following the movement in international contract prices.
In an advisory, Regasco president Arnel Ty said LPG prices will be rolled back by P2 per kilogram on Thursday, November 19, 2026.
Ty said the adjustments reflect the movement in international prices, citing optimism over the peace talks between the United States and Iran.
“Ang tanong ay maaari bang ito’y maging tuloy-tuloy? Ang sagot po namin diyan ay opo. ‘Yan pong mga series of rollback this month of November ay tuloy-tuloy,” he said.
Fuel prices dip Tuesday, Aug. 4; LPG prices rise in August
Petron Gasul LPG price up by P3/kg Aug. 1; gasoline, diesel rollback seen
LPG price rolls back by P5 per kilo
(The question is will this continue? Our answer is yes. The series of rollbacks this month of November will continue.)
Prices for December will largely be based on contract prices at the end of November, as reported by Saudi Aramco.
“Tayo pong mga LPG import terminal, sa kasalukuyan, lahat po ng dumarating nating mga produkto ay nandoon pa rin po sa presyong Nobyembre. Hindi pa po ito ‘yung presyong Disyembre,” he added.
(For LPG import terminals, currently, all of the products that arrive are still priced for the month of November. They do not reflect the prices for December yet.)
Other firms that earlier announced LPG price rollbacks for November include Petron which adjusted prices downward by P3.74 per kilogram on November 3; Filipino Energy Resources Corp. (EC Gas) and Pryce Gases by P4.00 per kilogram on November 3; and Seaoil by P3.74 per kilogram on November 5. — BM, GMA News

related.title: LPG carrier with 19 Filipinos on board struck in Black Sea off Bulgaria; crew rescued
related.text:
SOFIA, Bulgaria — A ship carrying liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) was struck in the Black Sea on Tuesday, Bulgarian authorities and the vessel's management company said, the latest in a spate of incidents thought to be fallout from the Ukraine war.
Nineteen crew members were rescued from the Gas Husky, the Bulgarian defense ministry said in a statement.
"The vessel was struck early this morning while sailing in the Black Sea, within Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone," the ship's Greek management company Stealth Maritime said, without specifying what it had been struck by.
At least 14 merchant ships have been hit by drones in the Black Sea off Romania and Bulgaria since early October, leaving more than 30 sailors dead or missing.
Ship that was hit by drones off Bulgaria sinks; Filipinos, other crew safe in Varna
Drones hit container ship off Bulgaria, crew including Filipinos safe and ashore
LPG tanker reported to have sunk off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast
Romania and Bulgaria have both pointed the finger at Russia over the attacks, though Bulgaria has underlined that there is no proof of who was behind them.
According to the Bulgarian transport ministry, the Gas Husky disappeared from radar shortly after midnight and its distress beacon was triggered at 8:02 am (06:02 GMT) about 50 nautical miles east of Byala.
The gas carrier, sailing under the Liberian flag, was transporting 3,400 tons of LPG from Egypt to Romania, with 19 Filipino sailors on board, the ministry said.
The incident comes just one day after another cargo ship, the Betul 8, capsized off Bulgaria after what rescued crew members described as a drone strike.
The Bulgarian transport ministry said 12 sailors were rescued from the Betul 8, which was carrying bulk wheat from Romania to Egypt. — Agence France Presse

article.text:
SOFIA, Bulgaria - A liquefied petroleum gas tanker that sank off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast on Tuesday had been struck by projectiles, a regional governor and maritime security sources said, joining a growing list of ships attacked in the area in recent weeks.
The Liberian-flagged Gas Husky was carrying 3,400 metric tons of LPG from Egypt to Romania when it sent a distress signal on Tuesday morning before starting to sink approximately 50 miles (80 km) east of Byala. All 19 Filipino crew members were rescued.
"There is no doubt about the number of strikes, there were four, but we have no confirmation from the sailors about the kind of drones used," Varna's regional governor Mario Smarkov said.
Two maritime security sources said the ship was hit by an unmanned system.
LPG carrier with 19 Filipinos on board struck in Black Sea off Bulgaria; crew rescued
LPG tanker reported to have sunk off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast
DMW reports over 1,200 OFWs repatriated from Saudi Arabia amid flight issues
The vessel's Greece-based manager did not respond to a request for comment on Wednesday.
The strike, a day after a cargo ship carrying wheat sank in the same area, is the latest in a spate of drone attacks that have left more than 20 seafarers missing and feared dead, raising concerns about the widening conflict between Russia and Ukraine in the Black Sea.
At least 17 vessels have been attacked off the coast of Bulgaria and Romania since mid-July, according to maritime security firm Diaplous.
The waters off the shores of the two NATO countries have become the primary route for shipments from Ukraine, one of the world's biggest grain exporters, the Black Sea ports of which have come under repeated fire from Russia since its invasion.
Romanian and Bulgarian officials have been cautious about ascribing blame for attacks near their coasts, although some have occasionally pointed fingers at Russia. Maritime security experts have also suggested Russian involvement, which Moscow denies.
Moscow has also accused Ukraine of striking Russian vessels in other parts of the Black Sea. — Reuters

deepDives.title: DMW mulls 'high-risk' label for southwestern Black Sea amid drone attacks
deepDives.summary: The DMW is preparing to recommend a review of existing maritime high-risk and warlike zone classifications to determine whether the southwestern Black Sea should be included.
reasons: reader relevance 3/3: DMW may label Black Sea high-risk; affects seafarer deployment
promoted to deep dive in place of "Peso weakens to P63.71:$1"

article.text:
The Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) is preparing to recommend a review of existing maritime high-risk and warlike zone classifications to determine whether the southwestern Black Sea should be included, following a reported drone attack on a liquefied petroleum gas tanker carrying 19 Filipino seafarers off the coast of Bulgaria.
Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac say Wednesday that reports of attacks on commercial vessels in the southwestern Black Sea have raised serious concerns over the safety of Filipino seafarers operating in the area.
“Nakikita na natin yung panganib sa southwestern side kaya yung ay papanukala natin ay isama yung southwestern side ng Black Sea sa pag-aralan, na isama yung southwestern side ng Black Sea sa high-risk or warlike zones,” Cacdac said.
(We saw that there is a risk in the southwestern part of the Black Sea, so our proposal is to include the area in the list of high-risk or war-like zones.)
DMW hopes for strong ASEAN declaration for safe recruitment amid scam hubs
Ship that was hit by drones off Bulgaria sinks; Filipinos, other crew safe in Varna
Drones hit container ship off Bulgaria, crew including Filipinos safe and ashore
“Rest assured we will make a recommendation na pag-aralan whether isasama na itong [to study whether to include the] southwestern part sa high-risk or warlike zone,” he added.
At least 14 merchant ships have been hit by drones in the Black Sea off Romania and Bulgaria since early October, leaving more than 30 sailors dead or missing.
Romania and Bulgaria have both pointed the finger at Russia over the attacks, though Bulgaria has underlined that there is no proof of who was behind them.
At present, the International Bargaining Forum (IBF) designates specific portions of the Black Sea as high-risk or warlike areas, including the northern region affected by the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war. The classifications do not cover the entire Black Sea.
Under existing maritime safety arrangements, Filipino seafarers who sail in areas designated as having risks are entitled to certain protections, including the right to refuse sailing, repatriation at the company's expense, additional compensation and enhanced security measures, depending on the applicable designation.
Cacdac said the recent incidents demonstrate the need to reassess whether these protections should be extended to waters farther southwest, including areas near Bulgaria and Romania.
The proposal remains subject to further study and the applicable processes for changing maritime risk classifications.
The Liberian-flagged LPG tanker Gas Husky sank on Tuesday, November 17, approximately 50 nautical miles off the coast of Bulgaria.
The vessel was reportedly traveling from Egypt and carrying some 3,400 metric tons of LPG when it encountered an emergency in the Black Sea.
The incident comes just one day after another cargo ship, the Betul 8, capsized off Bulgaria after what rescued crew members described as a drone strike.
According to Cacdac, reports received by the DMW indicated that the tanker was struck by drones, causing it to list and eventually sink.
The exact circumstances of the reported strike remain unclear, and the party responsible has not been conclusively identified.
The 19 Filipino crew members managed to abandon the vessel and board a life raft before it sank.
Bulgarian authorities subsequently launched a rescue operation, deploying helicopters to evacuate the stranded seafarers and bring them to safety.
Cacdac said two of the 19 Filipinos sustained minor injuries, but all crew members survived.
“Na-disembark sila at the right time, everybody ligtas at naisakay sa life raft at merong helicopter na sumagip sa kanila from the life raft. Ngayon, dinala na sila sa isang lugar, nasa hotel ngayon sa Bulgaria, at doon pupunta ang ating labor attaché,” he said.
(They disembarked at the right time and a helicopter retrieved them from the life raft. Now they are at a hotel in Bulgaria, and our labor attache will go theré.)
The DMW is coordinating with the Philippine labor attaché, the Department of Foreign Affairs and the vessel's Philippine manning agency to provide assistance and arrange the crew members' repatriation.
The incident underscores the risks to commercial shipping beyond the northern Black Sea, where maritime security concerns have persisted since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
The reported attack near Bulgaria has raised concerns that the dangers associated with the conflict could affect shipping routes beyond the areas currently classified as the most dangerous.
The DMW's proposed review could have implications for Filipino seafarers assigned to ships transiting the southwestern Black Sea, particularly in determining whether additional safety guarantees and the right to refuse sailing should apply.
Beyond the immediate safety concerns, Cacdac reiterated the Philippines' call for peace amid continuing conflicts that threaten overseas Filipino workers and international commercial shipping.
The appeal is consistent with the broader position advanced by the Philippines and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), which emphasizes dialogue, diplomacy, respect for international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes.
During the recently concluded 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits in Manila, regional leaders also emphasized the importance of maintaining peace and stability amid geopolitical tensions.
While ASEAN is not directly involved in resolving the Russia-Ukraine war, its longstanding principle of peaceful dispute settlement remains relevant to international conflicts whose consequences extend beyond the countries directly involved.
For the Philippines, these consequences are particularly significant because of the large number of Filipinos employed aboard international commercial vessels, including ships operating near conflict-affected waters in the Black Sea, the Strait of Hormuz and other parts of the Middle East.
The risks extend beyond disruptions to global trade and energy supplies, directly affecting the lives and livelihoods of Filipino maritime workers.
“Panawagan talaga ay magkaroon ng kapayapaan at manaig ang komersyo, manaig ang pagkakaroon ng malaya at mapayapang pamumuhay, lalo na yung mga OFWs natin doon, yung ligtas ang ating OFWs doon,” Cacdac said.
(Our call is for peace, and for commerce and freedom to prevail, especially for our OFWs.)
The DMW said it would continue coordinating with relevant agencies and maritime stakeholders to strengthen protections for Filipino seafarers as security threats affect commercial shipping routes. — BM, GMA News

article.text:
The Philippine peso weakened against the US dollar on Wednesday, weighed by geopolitical tensions abroad.
The local currency shed 4 centavos to close at P63.71:$1, from P63.64:$1 on Tuesday.
In a commentary, Rizal Commercial Banking Corp. chief economist Michael Ricafort attributed the peso's weakness to “some tensions between US and Iran.”
On Wednesday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he did not believe there was an imminent threat to Washington, following a CNN report citing US intelligence assessments on a possible Iranian plot involving a so-called dirty bomb in the US capital.

reasons: reader relevance 2/3: PH leads Asia-Pacific in identity fraud networks

article.text:
THE Philippines has emerged as a major hotspot for organized identity fraud in Asia-Pacific, recording the region’s largest number of detected fraud networks as criminals increasingly use interconnected accounts to carry out illicit activities.
The report, published by an AI-powered identity verification and compliance platform, Sumsub, analyzed more than 5.8 million fraud samples from the platform’s identity-verification and user-activity data.
Now in its sixth edition, Sumsub’s Identity Fraud Report 2026-2027 found that Asia-Pacific accounted for 33 percent of all fraud networks detected globally, more than any other region, and recorded close to a million confirmed fraud attempts, the highest of the six regions examined.
The Philippines represented 17 percent of the region’s networks, followed by India. The largest individual fraud network in the region was detected in Thailand, involving 3,018 linked users.
“Fraud in APAC isn’t rising everywhere at once. It is shifting between markets, techniques and stages of the customer lifecycle,” Sumsub APAC Vice President Penny Chai said.
“The region is home to some of the world’s most mature digital economies, alongside markets where digital services and organized scam operations are expanding quickly,” Chai added.
Sumsub found that around 2.4 percent of approved users in Asia-Pacific were linked to a detected fraud network.

GDP growth for the third quarter collapsed to 2.1 percent from 7.6 percent when Marcos took over. Inflation accelerated to 7.8 percent in October, the highest since 2023.
